newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says in talks to sell DG Bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says in talks to sell DG Bank stake.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry on Friday said it had started negotiations to sell its six percent stake in co-operative clearing bank DG Bank to a trustee, as a prelude to selling the stake on the market next year.
"We have already started discussing the sale with banks," the Ministry said in a statement, adding that two accounting firms had been engaged to assess the value of the stake.
The stake is understood to be worth some 500 million marks ($331.8 million).
The government's holding in the bank is currently deposited with the GNN Genossenschaftsholding, Berlin, a state-owned firm set up exclusively to hold the DG Bank stake.
Earlier the government said it wanted a trustee buyer to take on its remaining 35.7 percent stake in Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which should generate some 2.9 billion marks.
The shares will not be sold on the market until the second half of 1997.
